analysis.title: US Power & Utilities: Watt's On Tap Next Week
key_insights: The November 3 elections headline the week for US utilities, with affordability and data-center (large-load) growth central to the debate.
Governor races could reshape energy policy, infrastructure approvals and future utility commission appointments. BofA sees concentrated exposure in Texas, Georgia, Ohio, Oregon and Pennsylvania.
Texas load audits, permitting restrictions and the transmission debate likely extend uncertainty into 1H27 for SRE, CNP, AEP and VST.
Georgia's proposed development pause carries potential risk for SO. Both Ohio candidates support conditional moratoriums, relevant to AEP and FE.
Oregon's wildfire framework remains central to POR and AVA. Pennsylvania's regulatory review and Senate outcome might affect PPL, EXC and FE.
BofA sees disruption as likely more limited for CMS, DTE, EVRG and LNT, where legislative progress, existing contracts and established cost-allocation frameworks constrain policy changes.

Fifteen seats across nine elected commissions are contested on November 3. Party control could change in Georgia, Louisiana and North Dakota, though Republican control remains the North Dakota base case.

Democrats must win both contested seats to overturn the 3-2 Republican majorities in Georgia and Louisiana. Arizona could narrow to a 3-2 Republican majority, but the current commission is expected to decide APS's pending rate case before new commissioners take office.

PSC outcomes could affect SO's generation buildout, ETR's generation and resilience investment, and MDU's rate case and large-load approvals. Montana's elections are relevant to NWE/BKH merger oversight and Colstrip treatment.

Alabama's January commission expansion and new governor-appointed energy secretary create scope for a different regulatory agenda. Across PSC races, capital recovery, allowed returns and customer cost protections are the issues to watch.
22 covered companies report earnings the week of 11/2 to 11/6, including PEG, ETR, DUK, VST, SRE, SO, EVRG, DTE, ES and OKLO.

Regulatory calendar includes Virginia SCC merger hearings on the Dominion-NextEra combination (evidentiary hearing 11/17), an ERCOT SB6 large-load curtailment workshop on 11/6, and the ISO-NE Markets Committee capacity auction reform votes on 11/5.
FERC is running parallel show-cause proceedings on large-load interconnection and cost allocation across PJM, SPP, NYISO, MISO, CAISO and ISO-NE.

sector_views.rationale: The report is a weekly preview of elections, earnings and regulatory events. It gives no overall sector stance and flags election-driven risk to specific names (SO, AEP, FE, SRE, CNP, VST) and more limited risk for CMS, DTE, EVRG and LNT.

earnings_insights: 22 BofA-covered companies report the week of 11/2 to 11/6. Monday: PEG (11 am), ETR (11 am). Tuesday: TLN (8 am), OGS (11 am), PNW (11 am), DUK (10 am), ATO (10 am). Wednesday: AVA (10:30 am), SWX (11 am), WTRG (11 am), PPL (11 am), BKH (11 am), NWE (11 am), SRE (12 pm), SO (1 pm), AWR (2 pm), MDU (2 pm), SMR (5 pm), HASI (5 pm). Thursday: ES (9 am), EVRG (9 am), DTE (9 am), VST (10 am). Friday: OKLO (8:30 am), AEE (10 am). The exhibit's column layout is ambiguous in the text, so day assignments are approximate. No estimates are given in this note.
